goal:
`kvconf get` fails on a value that has a `#` inside double quotes. With this file:

```
[app]
title = "Issue #42: retry"
```

`go run ./cmd/kvconf get app.conf app.title` prints `kvconf: line 2: unterminated quoted value` instead of `Issue #42: retry`.

A `#` inside a double-quoted value is part of the value. The other quoting rules in the README must keep working:

- an unquoted value still ends at the first `#`: `port = 8080 # http` gives `8080`;
- after the closing quote, `# ...` is a comment: `title = "x" # note` gives `x`;
- inside quotes, `\"` is a double quote and `\\` is a single backslash: `path = "C:\\temp"` gives `C:\temp`.

`checks/quoted-hash.sh` reproduces the problem. The tests run with `go test ./...`.

criteria.statement: `kvconf get` prints `Issue #42: retry` for the reported file
criteria.baseline: it must fail on the input snapshot, reproducing the problem; interlock saw it fail there (run run-26104cd86f1d4e30)

criteria.statement: Every quoting rule in the task holds: a # inside quotes is kept, an unquoted value ends at #, a comment may follow the closing quote, and \" and \\ are escapes inside quotes

criteria.baseline: it must pass on the input snapshot, as a regression guard; interlock saw it pass there (run run-19681d4c99e847a3)

previous_result.summary:
I rewrote `parseValue` in `parser.go` so a quoted value is read up to its closing quote before any `#` handling. That keeps a `#` inside quotes, and `\"` and `\\` are unescaped there. After the closing quote only whitespace or a `# comment` is allowed. Unquoted values still end at the first `#`. I added `TestParseValueQuoting` in `parser_test.go` covering all four rules from the brief.

One behaviour I added that you didn't ask for: text after the closing quote that isn't a comment now returns "unexpected text after quoted value".

The repro check prints `Issue #42: retry` and `go test ./...` passes. I recorded `observed` for `repro`, `tested` for `regression`, and `tested` for `spec`. `repro` and `spec` still need the independent verifier.
